NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 8 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 1 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 30, 10:35 PM ET

Josh Allen is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 8 DraftKings main slate at 22.9 DraftKings points for $7,700, against Baltimore. Dak Prescott (22.0, $6,300) and Joe Burrow (21.0, $7,000) are next.

Dak Prescott returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.50 projected points per $1,000 at $6,300.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 30, 10:35 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 8

Josh Allen, BUF vs BAL ($7,700)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 22.9 DraftKings points at $7,700, the 3rd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 0.8 points clear of Dak Prescott. The model includes 6.7 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 2.97 projected points per $1,000, 15th of 20 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Allen averaged 22.8 points with a simulated floor of 9.3 and a ceiling of 41.9, and he holds 9% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 3-point favorite at home against Baltimore, with an implied team total of 28.75 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Dak Prescott, DAL vs ARI ($6,300)

Dak Prescott projects 2nd at the position with 22.0 DraftKings points at $6,300, 4th on the main slate overall. The salary works out to 3.50 projected points per $1,000, 1st of 20 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Prescott averaged 22.1 points with a simulated floor of 8.4 and a ceiling of 40.5, and he holds 18% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Dallas is a 7-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 30.75 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Value: Justin Herbert, LAC at LAR ($5,000)

Justin Herbert projects for 17.1 DraftKings points at $5,000, which works out to 3.42 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 20 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 4.2 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Herbert averaged 17.2 points with a simulated floor of 6.9 and a ceiling of 31.6, and he holds 3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Chargers are a 6.5-point underdog on the road against the Rams, with an implied team total of 19.5 in a game totaled at 45.5.
